name: forge
description: Claude Code plugins for making things and then checking them: design-forge for visual work, story-forge for long-form fiction, deck-forge for presentations, proof-forge for verifying exports. All built on the same idea — judgment stays with the model, and anything expressed as a number gets measured instead of eyeballed.

plugins.name: design-forge
plugins.description: Adversarial builder/critic loop, a measurement harness that computes what a screenshot cannot show (type ladder, worst-case accent count, WCAG contrast, target size), a licence-cleared asset library, a scroll-film site builder, and a three-pass prose de-slopper.

plugins.name: story-forge
plugins.description: A long-form fiction pipeline: braindump to dossier, outlining, story-hacking, drafting, a three-pass line edit that strips AI prose patterns, a continuity and chronology audit, and a final export that removes invisible provenance characters.

plugins.name: deck-forge
plugins.description: Build decks from shape primitives so they survive a Google Slides import fully editable, then measure them: type legibility from the AVIXA element-height model, WCAG contrast resolved against the real backdrop by z-order, and native-chart detection. The component library never creates a chart, and the audit catches one if you reach around it.

plugins.name: proof-forge
plugins.description: Verify what came out of the render. Compare two exports and mark exactly where they differ — video with timecoded markers and an EDL, stills with a bounding box, audio with a phase-invert null test. The threshold is derived from the pair being compared, so a routine re-encode produces nothing and one bad second produces one marker.
